sources.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415v6
sources.locator: Complete 239-page corpus, read sequentially; selected locators recorded in qc_r3.json.
contents: One-qubit and multi-qubit circuit models; universal finite gate sets and Solovay–Kitaev overview.
Uniform circuit families, BQP, circuit complexity and optimization/lower-bound discussion.

sources.title: Adriano Barenco et al., Elementary gates for quantum computation, arXiv:quant-ph/9503016
sources.locator: Complete 31-page paper, read sequentially; §§4–8 on Euler form, controlled gates, multi-control and two-level synthesis.
contents: Lemma 4.1 gives U(2)/SU(2) Euler factorization and §§5–7 give exact controlled-gate constructions and ancilla/resource tradeoffs.
§8 gives two-level/Givens-style arbitrary-unitary construction and dimension-count discussion.

sources.title: Vivek V. Shende, Stephen S. Bullock, and Igor L. Markov, Synthesis of Quantum Logic Circuits, arXiv:quant-ph/0406176
sources.locator: Complete 19-page paper, read sequentially; §§2–6, 8 and Appendix A.
contents: Exact CNOT synthesis via multiplexors/Quantum Shannon Decomposition, state synthesis and nearest-neighbor overhead.
Generic-unitary CNOT upper bound and cited dimension-count lower bound under exact no-ancilla circuit model.

sources.title: Christopher M. Dawson and Michael A. Nielsen, The Solovay–Kitaev Algorithm, arXiv:quant-ph/0505030v2
sources.locator: Complete 15-page paper, read sequentially; §§2–6 and appendices.
contents: Finite inverse-closed dense SU(d) gate-set hypotheses; SU(2) commutator recursion with error exponent 3/2, word-length exponent 3.97 and compressed compiler exponent 2.71.
The authors explicitly leave finite-precision arithmetic cost unanalyzed.

sources.title: Vadym Kliuchnikov, Dmitri Maslov, and Michele Mosca, Practical approximation of single-qubit unitaries by single-qubit quantum circuits, arXiv:1206.5236
sources.locator: Complete 23-page paper, read sequentially; §§2–5 and Appendices A–B.
contents: Exact single-qubit Clifford+T characterization by the dyadic cyclotomic ring and optimal exact H/T synthesis.
Multi-qubit ring characterization is conjectural here; controlled-T determinant obstruction and clean-ancilla implementation are distinguished.

sources.title: Neil J. Ross and Peter Selinger, Optimal ancilla-free Clifford+T approximation of z-rotations, arXiv:1403.2975
sources.locator: Complete 40-page paper, read sequentially; §§2–9 and appendices.
contents: Ancilla-free single-qubit Rz(θ) approximation in operator norm; factoring-oracle optimal T-count, near-optimal result under Hypothesis 8.3, and precision/runtime accounting.
The up-to-phase variant is isolated and proves only phases 1 and exp(iπ/8) need be considered for the Clifford+T problem.

sources.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, arXiv:0804.3401v1
sources.locator: Complete 44-page paper, read sequentially; §IV polynomial-time quantum computation and §VII.3 bounded-depth circuits.
contents: Formal promise-problem and polynomial-time-generated circuit family definitions, BQP acceptance thresholds and error-reduction statement.
Distinguishes polynomial-time-generated quantum circuits from other models; reports limited known depth/space relationships and no BQP-vs-classical separation.

sources.title: Dieter van Melkebeek and Thomas Watson, A Quantum Time-Space Lower Bound for the Counting Hierarchy, arXiv:0712.2545v1
sources.locator: Complete 25-page paper, read sequentially; §§2–3 and Appendices A–B.
contents: A model-specific BQTISP-to-PTISP simulation preserving time O(t polylog t) and space s+polylog t, including intermediate measurements.
The final MajSAT/MajMajSAT lower-bound theorem depends on the Allender et al. counting-hierarchy lower bound and must not be quoted without that separate supplier.
